article.story: Cincinnati (4-1) at West Virginia (3-3), Oct. 17 at 12 p.m. EDT. Opening Line: West Virginia by 1.5. Against the spread: West Virginia 2-3-1, Cincinnati 3-2. How to watch: TNT Key stats West Virginia Offense Overall: 480.3 yards per game (14th in FBS) Passing: 184.8 yards per game (113th) Rushing: 295.5 yards per game (4th) Scoring: 36.3 points per game (32nd) West Virginia Defense Overall: 460.8 yards per game (131st in FBS) Passing: 297.0 yards per game (136th) Rushing: 163.8 yards per game (98th) Scoring: 32.7 points per game (124th) Cincinnati Offense Overall: 427.6 yards per game (46th in FBS) Passing: 196.8 yards per game (98th) Rushing: 230.8 yards per game (12th) Scoring: 33.8 points per game (49th) Cincinnati Defense Overall: 401.6 yards per game (115th in FBS) Passing: 260.0 yards per game (124th) Rushing: 141.6 yards per game (69th) Scoring: 23.2 points per game (66th) Cincinnati ranks 121st in defensive third down percentage, allowing opponents to convert 45.6% of the time. West Virginia ranks 21st on offense, converting on 49.5% of third downs. West Virginia is 66th in the FBS with an even turnover margin, compared to Cincinnati's 15th-ranked +5 margin. Cincinnati ranks 105th in the FBS averaging 66.4 penalty yards per game, compared to West Virginia's 47th-ranked 51.5 per-game average. Team leaders West Virginia Passing: Michael Hawkins Jr., 1,055 yards, 7 TDs, 1 INT, 52.3 completion percentage Rushing: Cam Cook, 793 yards on 153 carries, 7 TDs Receiving: D.J. Epps, 393 yards on 14 catches, 4 TDs Cincinnati Passing: J.C. French, 949 yards, 6 TDs, 0 INTs, 69.9 completion percentage Rushing: Gi'Bran Payne, 392 yards on 62 carries, 2 TDs Receiving: JaVonnie Gibson, 267 yards on 18 catches, 3 TDs Last game West Virginia was beaten by Arizona 52-31 on Oct. 10. Hawkins passed for 219 yards on 11-of-28 attempts (39.3%) with no touchdowns and no interceptions. He also carried the ball 25 times for 98 yards and one rushing touchdown. Cook carried the ball 34 times for 141 yards and scored two touchdowns, adding one reception for 18 yards. Prince Strachan had five receptions for 121 yards. Cincinnati fell 34-7 to Arizona on Oct. 3. French led Cincinnati with 153 yards on 16-of-29 passing (55.2%) for no touchdowns and no interceptions. He also carried the ball nine times for 29 yards and one rushing touchdown. Payne had 24 rushing yards on 11 carries. Isaiah Johnson had six receptions for 60 yards. Next game West Virginia plays at TCU on Oct. 24. Cincinnati hosts No. 10 Texas Tech on Oct. 24.
